1.name: Spellcasting
1.notes:
You have learned to cast spells as a student of arcane magic.

Cantrips. You know three Wizard cantrips of your choice (Light, Mage Hand, and Ray of Frost are recommended). Whenever you finish a Long Rest, you can replace one of these cantrips with another Wizard cantrip of your choice. At Wizard levels 4 and 10, you learn one additional Wizard cantrip, as shown in the class table.

Spellbook. Your studies culminated in the creation of your spellbook. It is a Tiny object (3 pounds, 100 pages) that can be read only by you or by someone casting Identify. You determine its appearance and materials.
The book contains the level 1+ Wizard spells you know. It begins with six level 1 Wizard spells of your choice (Detect Magic, Feather Fall, Mage Armor, Magic Missile, Sleep, and Thunderwave are recommended).
Whenever you gain a Wizard level after 1, you add two Wizard spells of your choice to your spellbook. Each spell must be of a level for which you have spell slots, as shown in the Wizard Features table.

Spell Slots. The Wizard Features table shows how many spell slots you have to cast your level 1+ spells. You regain all expended spell slots when you finish a Long Rest.

Prepared Spells of Level 1+. You prepare a list of Wizard spells of level 1+ that you can cast. To start, choose four spells from your spellbook. Each prepared spell must be of a level for which you have spell slots.
The number of prepared spells increases as you gain Wizard levels, as shown in the Prepared Spells column of the Wizard Features table; whenever that number increases, you choose additional spells from your spellbook to match the new total.
If another Wizard feature gives you spells that are always prepared, those spells don’t count against the number of spells you can prepare, but they count as Wizard spells for you.

Changing Prepared Spells. Whenever you finish a Long Rest, you can change your list of prepared spells, replacing any of them with other spells from your spellbook.

Spellcasting Ability. Intelligence is your spellcasting ability for Wizard spells.

Spellcasting Focus. You can use an Arcane Focus or your spellbook as a Spellcasting Focus for your Wizard spells.

Expanding and Replacing a Spellbook. The spells you gain when leveling reflect your ongoing research, but you can also add spells you find:
• Copying a Spell into the Book. When you find a level 1+ Wizard spell, you can copy it into your spellbook if it is of a level you can prepare and you have the time and resources. Copying takes 2 hours and 50 GP per spell level. Once copied, you can prepare the spell like any other in your book.
• Copying the Book. You can copy spells from your spellbook into another book. This is faster because you already know the spells: it takes 1 hour and 10 GP per spell level.
• Replacing a Lost Book. If you lose your spellbook, you can use the same process to transcribe the Wizard spells you currently have prepared into a new book. Filling out the remainder of the new spellbook requires you to find additional spells. Many wizards keep a backup spellbook for this reason.

1.name: Ritual Adept
1.notes: You can cast any spell as a Ritual if the spell has the Ritual tag and is in your spellbook. You need not have the spell prepared, but you must read from your spellbook when casting it as a Ritual.

1.name: Arcane Recovery
1.notes:
You can regain some of your magical energy by studying your spellbook. When you finish a Short Rest, you can recover expended spell slots with a combined level equal to no more than half your Wizard level (round up), and none of the recovered slots can be level 6 or higher.
For example, as a level 4 Wizard, you can recover up to two levels’ worth of spell slots (one level 2 slot or two level 1 slots).
Once you use this feature, you can’t use it again until you finish a Long Rest.

2.name: Scholar
2.notes: In addition to your magical studies, you specialized in another field of study. Choose one of the following skills in which you have proficiency: Arcana, History, Investigation, Medicine, Nature, or Religion. You gain Expertise in the chosen skill.

3.name: Illusion Savant
3.notes:
Add two free level 1–2 Illusion Wizard spells to your spellbook.
Whenever you gain a new level of spell slots, add one free Illusion spell of a level you can cast.

3.name: Improved Illusions
3.notes:
You can cast Illusion spells without Verbal components.
If an Illusion spell you cast has a range of 10+ feet, its range increases by 60 feet.
You learn Minor Illusion (or another Wizard cantrip if you already know it); it doesn't count against cantrips known.
When casting Minor Illusion, you can create both a sound and an image with one casting, and you can cast it as a Bonus Action.

5.name: Memorize Spell
5.notes: Whenever you finish a Short Rest, you can study your spellbook and replace one of the level 1+ Wizard spells you have prepared for your Spellcasting feature with a different level 1+ Wizard spell from your spellbook.

6.name: Phantasmal Creatures
6.notes:
You always have Summon Beast and Summon Fey prepared.
When you cast either spell, you can treat it as an Illusion spell; the summoned creature appears spectral.
You can cast the Illusion version of each spell without expending a spell slot, but the creature's Hit Points are halved for that casting.
Once you cast either spell without a spell slot, you must finish a Long Rest before you can cast that spell in this way again.

10.name: Illusory Self
10.notes:
When a creature hits you with an attack roll, you can use a Reaction to create an illusory duplicate between you and the attacker; the attack automatically misses, then the illusion dissipates.
Once used, you must finish a Short or Long Rest to use it again, or you can restore its use by expending a level 2+ spell slot (no action required).

1.name: Bardic Inspiration
1.notes:
You can supernaturally inspire others through words, music, or dance. This inspiration is represented by your Bardic Inspiration die, which starts as a d6.

Using Bardic Inspiration. As a Bonus Action, you can inspire a creature within 60 feet of yourself who can see or hear you. That creature gains one Bardic Inspiration die. A creature can have only one Bardic Inspiration die at a time.

Within the next hour, when the creature fails a D20 Test, it can roll the Bardic Inspiration die and add the result to the d20, potentially turning failure into success. The die is expended when rolled.

Number of Uses. You can use Bardic Inspiration a number of times equal to your Charisma modifier (minimum of one) and regain all uses when you finish a Long Rest.

At Higher Levels. The Bardic Inspiration die increases to a d8 at level 5, a d10 at level 10, and a d12 at level 15.

1.name: Spellcasting
1.notes:
You have learned to cast spells through your bardic arts.

Cantrips. You know two Bard cantrips of your choice. Dancing Lights and Vicious Mockery are recommended. You learn more cantrips at Bard levels 4 and 10. When you gain a Bard level, you may replace one cantrip you know.

Spell Slots. You use the Bard Features table to determine how many spell slots you have to cast level 1+ spells.

Prepared Spells. You prepare a list of Bard spells equal to the Prepared Spells column of the Bard Features table. Prepared spells must be of a level for which you have spell slots.

Changing Spells. When you gain a Bard level, you may replace one prepared spell.

Spellcasting Ability. Charisma is your spellcasting ability.

Spellcasting Focus. You may use a Musical Instrument as a Spellcasting Focus.

2.name: Expertise
2.notes: You gain Expertise in two of your skill proficiencies. Performance and Persuasion are recommended. At Bard level 9, you gain Expertise in two additional skills.

2.name: Jack of All Trades
2.notes: You can add half your Proficiency Bonus (round down) to any ability check you make using a skill for which you lack proficiency and that does not otherwise add your Proficiency Bonus.

3.name: Combat Inspiration
3.notes:
Your Bardic Inspiration can enhance both offense and defense in battle.

Defense: When a creature with your Bardic Inspiration die is hit by an attack, it can use its Reaction to roll the die and add the result to its AC against that attack, potentially causing the attack to miss.

Offense: After a creature hits with an attack roll, it can roll the Bardic Inspiration die and add the result to the attack's damage.

3.name: Martial Training
3.notes:
You gain proficiency with Martial weapons, Medium armor, and Shields.

You can use a Simple or Martial weapon as a Spellcasting Focus for Bard spells.

traits.name: Gnomish Cunning
traits.notes: You have Advantage on Intelligence, Wisdom, and Charisma saving throws.

traits.name: Gnomish Lineage
traits.notes: You are part of a lineage that grants you supernatural abilities. Choose one of the following options; whichever one you choose, Intelligence, Wisdom, or Charisma is your spellcasting ability for the spells you cast with this trait (choose the ability when you select the lineage):

subrace.name: Forest Gnome
subrace.notes: You know the Minor Illusion cantrip. You also always have the Speak with Animals spell prepared. You can cast it without a spell slot a number of times equal to your Proficiency Bonus, and you regain all expended uses when you finish a Long Rest. You can also use any spell slots you have to cast the spell.

feats.notes: Two Cantrips. You learn two cantrips of your choice from the Cleric, Druid, or Wizard spell list. Intelligence, Wisdom, or Charisma is your spellcasting ability for this feat's spells (choose when you select this feat).Level 1 Spell. Choose a level 1 spell from the same list you selected for this feat's cantrips. You always have that spell prepared. You can cast it once without a spell slot, and you regain the ability to cast it in that way when you finish a Long Rest. You can also cast the spell using any spell slots you have.Spell Change. Whenever you gain a new level, you can replace one of the spells you chose for this feat with a different spell of the same level from the chosen spell list.
feats.name: Magic Initiate (Druid)

feats.notes: Blindsight. You have Blindsight with a range of 10 feet.Fog of War. You exploit the distractions of battle, gaining Advantage on any Dexterity (Stealth) check you make as part of the Hide action during combat.Sniper. If you make an attack roll while hidden and the roll misses, making the attack roll doesn't reveal your location.
feats.name: Skulker

feats.notes: Armor Training. You gain training with Light armor and Shields.
feats.name: Lightly Armored
